Protocol tables:
- Component error: C2 is worse than TreeHFD at most rho values, with larger spread. It is slightly lower only at rho 0.9 (2.82 vs 3.05), within the spread. TreeSHAP has much larger component error from rho 0.25 upward and is slightly lower at rho 0 (7.94 vs 8.52).
- Rank stability: C2 is below TreeHFD at all rho values and on Airfoil, so deeper selection did not make importances more stable.
- Rank agreement with the true importances: C2 is higher than TreeHFD at rho 0.75 and 0.95, and lower at rho 0, 0.25 and 0.5. The differences are mixed and mostly small relative to the spread.
- Residual MSE against the fitted ensemble: TreeSHAP is essentially zero, as expected for an exact additive attribution of the model. C2 is above TreeHFD at most settings.
- Runtime: TreeSHAP is far faster than both. C2 is faster than TreeHFD on Analytical and slower on Airfoil.

## Limitations

- The loop was crude. Only 1 of 3 ideas was run, and the ideas were produced and implemented by a language model. Only 3 seeds were used, on two datasets and one model configuration (xgboost, 100 trees). C2 was tuned only over depth_variable values 1-3.
- Research question coverage: the experiments address component error against known components and bootstrap rank stability as rho rises from 0 to 0.95, but only on the one synthetic Analytical function, with xgboost only. Random forests were not tested. The comparison on other public datasets (California housing, Adult) was not done. Airfoil was the only real dataset and has no true components, so only stability and residual MSE are available there.
- The main-table Residual MSE is held-out and is not comparable to the in-sample baseline numbers.
- Low residual MSE for TreeSHAP reflects its additive exactness, not accurate components. Component error shows otherwise.
- This report shows that C2 did not help in this setup. It does not show that deeper variable selection cannot help.
